findings_and_connected_questions.classification: new current conditional source finding that advances earlier q1881; exact alias and repair owner remain central
findings_and_connected_questions.title: Site-only lookup rejects separately owned exact pins after a lead is shared
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: Gateway pin projection scans qualifying exact uncorrected leads and keys the output by (owner_character_id, case_site_id). Sharing an investigation lead with a living co-located party recipient inserts another lead for that recipient with all source fields otherwise preserved and does not delete the sender lead. When both source and copied lead meet valid site, provenance, presentation and exact-coordinate predicates, two owner-specific pins for one site can coexist. The site-only query returns both under normal gateway SQL semantics; query_one rejects more than one and resolve_location maps that error to Unavailable. The schedule preview separately uses the existing site-and-owner query.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires distinct owners, successful authorized lead sharing, an exact current uncorrected source lead, passing provenance/presentation checks and expected SQL response. A current database instance, HTTP request and player impact were not observed. A one-row site-only lookup also needs viewer-identity policy, but this evidence does not establish unauthorized disclosure.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Carry the actual observer identity to each case-site pin lookup and reconcile callers with exact owner scope, missing versus unavailable, and current observation/time policy. Preserve intentional sharing and consent; verify endpoint and view contracts after audit/implementation are authorized.

TravelEdgeCache commits any successful empty vector into its process-local OnceCell and retries only errors; its existing test source explicitly treats an empty response array as a successful empty cache.

nonfindings.text: query_one explicitly rejects more than one row and accepts zero or one; it does not silently choose the first row within a result. The multi-owner bug comes from an under-scoped query against an owner-keyed view.

String query macros quote literals and double apostrophes; numeric IDs are formatted as u64 and table/key prefixes are static. The actual SQL dialect and all callers remain open; no injection conclusion follows from this alone.

SATS generated rows check named top-level columns, row/product arity, sum shape/tag and byte hex before serde; immutable preconditions guard the named-element expects. No ordinary panic, runtime schema drift, or forged response is claimed.

Byte-array hex and identity numeric hex use different native representations; capitalized sum and lowercased option names plus explicit SATS Option/unit variants are foreign boundary adapters, not automatically obsolete compatibility paths.

Query metrics share non-reset atomic counters and measure request-send elapsed until headers; snapshots need not be an atomic pair or per-request trace. Existing current startup uses a zero delta against the same baseline; no measured latency or isolated attribution guarantee established.
Existing topology test source includes a local HTTP fixture and asserts [] successful empty cache; it was read but never run. No conclusion that [] is forbidden by the actual service contract.
